//: Drop these into the settings of the Claude Code session you drive chargehand from (not the runner's). Reading is allowed; every mutating command asks, which prompts in every permission mode including auto and bypassPermissions.
//rules: Each ask rule leads with a wildcard rather than anchoring on the program name. A Bash rule matches the command text, not the program behind it, so an anchored 'Bash(chargehand cancel:*)' gates 'chargehand cancel X' and misses both '/usr/local/bin/chargehand cancel X' and "sh -c 'chargehand cancel X'". An assistant that ran 'which chargehand' and used the answer produces the second form without trying to evade anything. The allow rules stay anchored on purpose: a read that falls outside them prompts, which is the harmless direction to fail in.
